Let’s dive into Chapter 6: Leveraging Sources of Power.
Now that you’ve laid the groundwork with a clear diagnosis, guiding policy, and coherent action, it’s time to look for those unique advantages that can really tip the scales in your favor.
In strategy, power isn’t just about pushing harder or being the biggest player in the room. It’s about finding those smart leverage points—places where a well-placed effort creates the biggest impact.
So, what kinds of power can you tap into? Let’s walk through a few that show up again and again.
Scale is a big one. If you’re part of a large organization, you can spread your costs over more customers, strike better deals with suppliers, or invest in things that smaller rivals just can’t afford.
Then there are network effects. Think about how a social media platform becomes more valuable as more people join, or how a payment system is easier to use when all your friends and merchants are on board. The more users, the stronger your position.
Don’t underestimate the power of brand and reputation either. A trusted name isn’t just a nice-to-have—it can open doors, help you charge higher prices, and make new customers feel more comfortable choosing you.
Sometimes it’s all about having unique capabilities. Maybe you’ve got specialized skills, exclusive access to resources, or technology nobody else has. Those can set you apart in a big way.
And of course, positioning matters—being in the right place at the right time, whether that’s a physical location, a moment in the market, or a technological niche, can be a game-changer.
Picture this: a small software company facing off against industry giants. Instead of trying to outspend or out-scale the big guys, they focus on a niche market. Their deep expertise and close relationships with customers become their secret weapon. By doubling down on what makes them special, they build real loyalty—and carve out a space the big players just can’t reach.
So, how do you make the most of your sources of power?
First, identify your unique strengths. What do you do better than anyone else? Find ways to shine a spotlight on those strengths.
Next, exploit asymmetries. Where do your strengths line up with a competitor’s weakness? That’s where you want to focus your energy.
And finally, build on success. Use your early wins as a launching pad. Reinvest where you already have an edge, and let that momentum carry you forward.
Here’s a metaphor that really brings it home: think of strategy like a game of judo. You’re not trying to overpower your opponent—you’re using their weight and movement to your own advantage. By truly understanding the landscape and the sources of power available to you, you can create strategies that aren’t just effective, but sustainable in the long run.
